plates.side_label: 1763–1988 TIMELINE · 8–10 DAY PLATELET BLOCKADE · 23% HEART-ATTACK MORTALITY DROP (ISIS-2)
plates.quality_reason: Flow-first: a teach diagram, chart, counter or timeline is a £0 code graphic. No Flow mint.
plates.reference: Own code graphic: on period paper, the 5-date timeline completes: 25 Apr 1763 (Reverend Edward Stone reports curing 50 fever patients with dried white willow bark to the Royal Society) · 1828–1838 (Buchner, Leroux & Raffaele Piria isolate salicin and salicylic acid) · 10 Aug 1897 (Felix Hoffmann synthesises pure acetylsalicylic acid — Aspirin — at Bayer in Elberfeld) · 23 Jun 1971 (John Vane discovers aspirin blocks prostaglandin synthesis via the COX enzyme) · 1975–1988 (Roth & Majerus prove irreversible platelet COX-1 acetylation; ISIS-2 trial of 17,187 patients proves low-dose aspirin cuts heart-attack mortality by 23%).

teach_overlay.label: 1763–1988 TIMELINE & ISIS-2 TRIAL (17,187 PATIENTS: −23% HEART-ATTACK MORTALITY WITH LOW-DOSE ASPIRIN)
teach_overlay.detail: Animated 5-date timeline (25 Apr 1763 → 1975–1988) alongside 8–10 day irreversible platelet thromboxane A2 blockade (75–81 mg dose) and the 1988 ISIS-2 trial of 17,187 patients showing a 23% drop in vascular mortality
teach_overlay.scale: one tiny seventy-five-milligram aspirin tablet disables a blood platelet's clotting factory for its entire ten-day life — cutting heart-attack deaths by nearly a quarter
